narrative_summary: The five-to-six session base above the 7/08-7/17 swing lows failed decisively today: SPX closed 7,316.15 (-1.52%), in the bottom third of its range, below the 20-day, 50-day, the entire 23.6-61.8% fib band and the lower Bollinger Band, landing exactly on the re-anchored liquidation-caution level of 7,300.16. Monte Carlo now reads 78.08% down-first with a 2-day median to 7,300 and a 57% conditional cascade to 7,149.64 if it gives way — the most bearish skew of this arc and a sixth straight session failing every regime threshold. VIX has broken above 20 into the elevated-risk regime without a capitulation spike, ERP has collapsed to 0.06% at the valuation ceiling with the re-entry floor (7,399.45) now above spot, and McClellan breadth (854) plus net new highs (1.53) continue to refuse confirmation. The long-term bull skeleton (50-day above a rising 200-day, extension compressed to +4.29%) is intact, but nothing in the confirmation stack supports deployment: defensive patience, no adds, and monitoring 7,300 as the pivot between an orderly retest and a cascade toward 7,150.

Treat 7,300.16 as the pivot — a clean break opens the nervous zone 7,149.64 with a 57% conditional cascade; require a VIX spike-and-reverse plus 3 of 4 re-entry checklist conditions (close above prior high, RSI turning up from depressed, breadth improving, VIX reversing) before any re-entry.

confirming_evidence: Long-term bull skeleton intact: 50-day (7,468.1) remains above a rising 200-day (7,015.5), and the 3-year chart shows an unbroken sequence of higher highs and higher lows with price still far above the 200-day (07_spx_3year.png).

Extension has compressed to +4.29% above the 200-day — normal-extension territory, which justifies full drift (mu 0.09) and removes the mean-reversion penalty that governed earlier sessions (05_spx_6month.png).
Rally Exhaustion Score is Low with realized 20-day vol at only 10.48%, so probabilities are used at face value rather than discounted — the decline is orderly, not a volatility-driven unwind.

Credit remains benign: junk-vs-IG spread at 1.29 sits essentially on its 1.286 one-year average with no sustained widening, so credit is not confirming a systemic risk event (15_junk_bond_spread.png).

Sentiment is already depressed rather than complacent: Fear & Greed at 32 in the fear zone and put/call at 0.84 near the top of its one-year range, indicating hedging demand rather than the deep complacency that precedes trim windows (08_fear_greed_index.png, 12_put_call_ratio.png).

Daily RSI-14 has fallen to roughly the high-30s and MFI to the mid-to-high-40s — approaching but not yet in the buy-watch band, leaving room for a washout that could set up a genuine re-entry (04_spx_3month.png, 05_spx_6month.png).

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: The 50-day remains above a rising 200-day and extension has compressed to a healthy +4.29%, so the multi-quarter uptrend structure is undamaged and the pullback is proportionate.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: McClellan Volume Summation has slid to 854, its cycle-low reference, and net new 52-week highs are just 1.53 and falling — participation has been contracting the entire time price was churning near highs, the classic narrow-leadership topping signature.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: When breadth and credit both diverge from price, elevate caution even if price has not yet broken down; falling breadth near highs is a topping warning.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Full drift (mu 0.09) applies at only +4.29% extension and the 60-day drift path projects 7,464.85 — back at the 50-day — implying time is on the bulls' side once the retest completes.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: Adjusted prob_up_first is only 21.92% versus 78.08% down-first with a 2-day median to 7,300.16 and 19 days to 7,525.94; the setup fails every regime threshold (65/70/75) for a sixth consecutive session.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: Never use the Monte Carlo output in isolation; if the adjusted probability does not meet the regime threshold, the setup is not actionable.

conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: When VIX is above 20, reduce confidence in moving-average support; a correction without a volatility spike is orderly rather than capitulative.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Price has pierced the lower Bollinger Band with intraday RSI dropping near 20 — a mechanically oversold condition that often precedes a bounce (01_spx_intraday.png).
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: The close landed in the bottom third of the daily range with intraday price sliding from ~7,450 to ~7,318 into the bell and daily MFI turning down through the 50s — a distribution-style close confirming institutional selling pressure into the close, not stabilization.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: A close in the bottom third of the range is a weak/distribution-style close; MFI falling during a decline confirms institutional selling pressure.

primary_tension: A mechanically intact long-term bull skeleton (50-day above a rising 200-day, extension compressed to a benign +4.29%, Low exhaustion, full drift, neutral credit, depressed sentiment) is colliding with a decisive short-term breakdown and total confirmation failure: price sliced the six-session base, both July swing lows, the 20/50-day cluster and the lower Bollinger Band to close in the bottom third of its range right on the 7,300.16 liquidation-caution level; Monte Carlo is 78.08% down-first with a 2-day median to that level and a 57% cascade to 7,149.64; VIX has broken above 20 into the elevated-risk regime without a capitulation spike; ERP has collapsed to 0.06% at the valuation ceiling with the re-entry floor now above spot; and McClellan breadth sits at its cycle-low reference with net new highs at 1.53.
